title: Evaluation of a Hearing Device Kit 1-2026
official: Evaluation of a Hearing Device Kit 1-2026
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate outcomes with a hearing device kit. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does use of the hearing device kit address challenging listening situations identified by participants while providing a satisfactory user experience?
* How does participants' performance with the hearing device kit compare to performance in the unaided condition?

Participants will:

* Use the hearing device kit for approximately 2 weeks.
* Visit the clinic for the initial fitting and follow-up testing at the end of the study. Additional study visits may take place, as needed.
* Complete questionnaires to identify challenging listening situations and provide feedback on their experience with the devices.
* Complete lab testing to assess speech understanding in the presence of background noise and provide subjective feedback on device features.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults (aged 18 - 99 years).
* Have mild to profound bilateral, primarily sensorineural hearing loss (within fitting range of the investigational devices).
* Current hearing aid user (for at least 3 months).
* Cognitive and functional capability to consent to study procedures, operate the controls for the devices, and comply with all directions during the study.
* Ability to fluently read, write, and speak in English.
* Willingness to comply with all study requirements, including willingness to wear devices for a minimum of 8 hours a day.
* Good overall health, including healthy outer ear with no excessive wax/debris.
* Ear canal size/shape must accommodate appropriate fitting of the hearing aids.
* Use/ownership of a smartphone for Bluetooth audio streaming.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Significant medical conditions that, in the opinion of the investigators, are likely to interfere with study procedures or confound study outcomes.
* Contraindications to investigational device use in this study: known hypersensitivity or allergy to investigational product.
* Limited ability to describe listening impressions/experiences and the use of hearing aids.
* Dexterity concerns that inhibit ability to insert/remove hearing aids.
* Acute tinnitus (\<3 months of onset).
* Deformity of the ear (i.e., closed ear canal, absence of the auricle).
* Neural hearing loss (i.e., retro-cochlear pathologies).
* Inability to attend scheduled visits (mobility and/or scheduling).
